absent: Numeric defaults and valid ranges for watchdog timeout and watchdog interval and their configuration paths.
Full structure layouts and sizes beyond the observed rescue and runnable and slice and weight and queue fields.
Bypass mode entry and exit semantics and broader slice and dispatch lifecycle outside tick and rescue.
Semantics of optional scheduler callbacks beyond tick and weight and affinity and dump and group init and exit.
Allocation failure cleanup scope for arena objects beyond returning out of memory.
Locking and lifetime rules for scheduler root pointer and exit information and dump buffer sizing.
Meaning and lifecycle of switching flag and rejected count and hotplug and enable sequences.
Complete event list and counter semantics and per processor dump selection details.

findings.text: Rescue flushing exists in two build variants sharing a name. The full variant ends any active rescue occupancy and returns queued rescue tasks to processor local dispatch while disarming the related timer. The header variant is an empty operation for builds without rescue support.
Rescue flushing requires the caller to already hold the runqueue lock. The holding is asserted on entry and maintained across slice termination and queue draining and timer cancellation.

Stall detection walks runnable membership under runqueue locking with interrupts saved. It compares current time against each member runnable timestamp plus a configurable timeout. On expiry it attributes blame to the queue drainer except for processor local queues before requesting scheduler exit with stall indication and reporting that a timeout occurred.

Periodic watchdog maintenance records a liveness timestamp and probes each online processor for stalls with voluntary rescheduling between probes. It stops early after the first stall and requeues itself after a configurable interval unless that interval holds its maximum disabling value.

Tick handling for this class refreshes current execution accounting and forces immediate slice expiry while bypassing because slice tracking is untrusted. Otherwise it invokes an optional scheduler tick callback when present and requests rescheduling whenever remaining slice is empty.

Weight changes are ignored for tasks that are dead and finished or not currently enabled in this class to avoid notifying after disable. Otherwise the class converts generic load weight into group scale and stores it in task scheduler state and notifies an optional weight callback when implemented.

Entry into this class enables task tracking and refreshes processor affinity in the scheduler when identifier handling does not apply and the affinity callback exists. Exit disables tracking except when task state already indicates untracked handoff to a parent where disabling is skipped to avoid validation failure. Priority change and post entry notifications are defined as empty.

Group serialization has a full and an empty variant. The full variant nests global group exclusion with a scheduler group operations write lock when group scheduling is enabled and releases in reverse order. Alternate variants are no operation and the root lookup returns either the default hierarchy root or null depending on build.

Dispatch queue teardown releases per processor deferred requeue state after verifying emptiness with a one time warning and repair and then frees per processor storage. Final release is ordered through interrupt work to deferred callback to deallocation to allow safe use from contexts that already hold scheduler locks.

User queue destruction refuses queues that still hold tasks with a scheduler error and removes the queue from lookup and invalidates its identifier to block further submission and defers actual freeing through shared interrupt work. Lookup is protected by deferred reclamation read protection and mutation by queue spinlock with interrupts saved.

Group initialization walks online groups in ancestor first order and teardown walks in descendant first order while relying on external group exclusion. Initialization invokes an optional per group callback with weight and bandwidth and idle parameters and records scheduler association and an initialized flag. Teardown clears association for all visited groups and invokes an optional exit callback only for those previously initialized. Alternate variants are empty with success return for init.

Global scheduler user visible surface exposes five read only entries for overall state and whole system switching flag and rejected count and hotplug sequence and enable sequence grouped as one attribute set. A separate per scheduler entry exposes the operations name and another entry exposes event counters with one line per event.

Kernel arena object management applies only to identifier based schedulers with an arena pool and requires hotplug exclusion by the caller. Allocation creates one scratch affinity mask per possible processor plus a shared online mask and initializes them for the possible range and publishes the online view from the active set under deferred reclamation protection. Release frees the shared mask and each scratch mask and clears the scratch pointer.

Scheduler destruction runs as deferred work after inactivity and covers interrupt work synchronization and helper termination and timer shutdown and mask release and sub scheduler group and object release and per processor deferred and kick list validation with capacity sync discard and bypass queue teardown and node and shard release and remaining user queue destruction by hash walk and hash teardown and exit information and arena release and sub count decrement and final deallocation.

Scheduler to group association is accessed through a small helper that returns the stored group pointer in sub scheduler builds and null otherwise without additional locking or validation in the shown fragments.

Partition shard release tolerates null inputs and frees an optional outgoing affinity mask sized for the shard processor count when present and then frees the shard container. Collection release walks the configured shard count and frees the pointer array when allocated.

Discarding pending capacity synchronization for a processor requires no caller lock and internally serializes with the runqueue lock while atomically extracting the shared lockless list and returning unrelated entries and marking the target entry detached. It then waits with processor relaxation until the entry is observed detached to cover batches held privately across unlocks. An alternate header variant is empty.
Sub scheduler presence tracking decrements a global static branch only for non root levels with an empty alternate for builds without sub scheduler support.
Scheduler object release does not free directly but initializes and queues deferred work that performs full teardown to allow the final reference drop to occur in any context.

State dumping serializes with a dedicated dump spinlock with interrupts saved and returns early when dumping is disabled. It captures monotonic and tick time and identifies root versus sub scheduler and reports exit kind and location with reason and backtrace or debug trigger and invokes an optional scheduler dump callback and emits stalled processors first to survive truncation followed by remaining processors and then emits event counters and applies a truncation marker when the bounded buffer overflows.

Dump formatting tolerates zero length buffers without warning and always terminates lines and mirrors lines to a trace event when enabled using a lock protected static buffer. It formats backtraces with symbolic addresses and a caller prefix and initializes callback dump context with current processor identity and output position under disabled interrupts assertion.

Observed runqueue scheduler state includes a rescue area with a current task pointer and a dispatch queue with list membership and a timer plus a runnable list with membership node and a deferred capacity sync list with its lock and kick work. Observed task scheduler state includes slice and weight and runnable timestamp and queue pointer.

Stall probing holds the target runqueue lock with interrupts saved across root lookup and list walk. Queue destruction holds deferred reclamation read protection across lookup and queue spinlock with interrupts saved across occupancy check and removal. State dumping holds a global dump spinlock with interrupts saved across the whole emission.

Stall handling keeps owner blame for processor local consumption and moves blame to the draining scheduler for other queues. Teardown ordering assumes bypass mode blocks new deferrals and kicks with one time warnings rather than enforced waiting except for capacity sync discard which waits for detachment.
